note: vespera-bridge: a WebFlux explicit stream that fails before its first flush hint now answers the proxy 500 instead of committing Rust's status, headers and a partial body. A servlet ASYNC client disconnect is reported as 499 (no WARN) like WebFlux. A WebFlux multipart body consumed by a WebFilter answers 500 instead of reaching Rust empty. An unparsable Rust Content-Type passes through ASYNC like the other modes. The proxy restores the caller's MDC request id, a buffered read with Content-Length 0 and Transfer-Encoding honours the cap, and a cyclic cause chain no longer hangs the async completion. A DIRECT stash entry cleared by a runtime shutdown answers the retryable 503. The native loader checks the ancestors of the extraction directory and reports an invalid vespera.native.dir as UnsatisfiedLinkError without leaking the resource stream. VesperaClient rejects a '#' in rawQuery, encodes lone surrogates as U+FFFD in query and body, and rejects decode-only charsets clearly. Gradle plugin: bundleNativeLib, verifyNativeLibs and the native jar tasks read the vespera block lazily, and arch aliases the bridge loader never looks up (arm64, amd64, armv7) are rejected. Doc and test fixes.
